conflicts.description: Discrepancy in table and field naming conventions between Synthea and OMOP (e.g. Synthea 'patients' vs OMOP 'person', Synthea 'encounters' vs OMOP 'visit_occurrence', Synthea 'conditions' vs OMOP 'condition_occurrence', Synthea 'medications' vs OMOP 'drug_exposure', Synthea 'observations' vs OMOP 'measurement'/'observation', Synthea 'organizations' vs OMOP 'care_site').
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to standard snake_case canonical clinical domain models aligned with OMOP Common Data Model terminology and structure.

conflicts.description: Field naming differences for identical clinical concepts (e.g., patient identifier 'patient' vs 'person_id', provider identifier 'provider' vs 'provider_id', encounter identifier 'encounter' vs 'visit_occurrence_id').

Synthea models cost fields ('cost') and utilization counts as strings, whereas OMOP represents costs in the 'cost' table with numerical representations or strings, and vocabulary_name as an integer in OMOP metadata.
conflicts.resolution: Harmonized financial and quantity amounts to numeric types (number) and names/identifiers to appropriate string types.

conflicts.description: Synthea observation 'value' is string while OMOP splits into 'value_as_number' (number) and 'value_as_string' (string).
conflicts.resolution: Retained distinct value type fields (value_as_number, value_as_string, and value_as_concept_id) to accurately support both continuous and categorical results.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores medical concepts as source vocabulary code strings (e.g., SNOMED, RxNorm, CVX, LOINC) accompanied by text descriptions directly in the event tables, whereas OMOP maps clinical events to standardized integer Concept IDs and retains source values in dedicated source value columns.
conflicts.resolution: Included both concept ID foreign keys for standardized terminology mapping and source value/code string fields with explicit provenance mapping to the Synthea source codes.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds geographic address attributes (street address, city, state, zip) directly within patient, provider, and organization records, whereas OMOP normalizes geographic location details into a separate 'location' table referenced via 'location_id'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified address attributes into a normalized 'location' resource and linked person, provider, and care_site entities to it via 'location_id'.

conflicts.description: Synthea models financial costs as embedded columns inside clinical event records (encounters, medications, immunizations, procedures), whereas OMOP consolidates costs into an independent 'cost' table.
conflicts.resolution: Retained a consolidated 'cost' resource capable of referencing any domain event through domain and event foreign identifiers, while also supporting direct event association.

conflicts.description: Synthea captures allergies, conditions, medications, procedures, and imaging studies as direct 1:N relations with encounter and patient, whereas OMOP supports micro-level hierarchies (e.g. visit_occurrence to visit_detail) and composite episode groupings.
conflicts.resolution: Structured target entities to support both direct visit/encounter linking and extended visit_detail/episode associations without loss of granularity.

conflicts.description: Synthea tables like allergies, immunizations, conditions, and procedures lack explicit primary key designations in schema definitions, whereas OMOP standardizes surrogate event primary keys (e.g. condition_occurrence_id, procedure_occurrence_id).
conflicts.resolution: Designated canonical primary keys across all unified target entity tables with synthetic keys where missing in source records.
